<!-- pr-reviewer: 74c5ba8b8bc37256e8451d2ef65aad4ef2c52354 -->
**Needs changes before merge**

Thanks for picking up the second half of #266. The shape is right: it reads the one `tool_law::cutting_radius`, it only removes `Gouge` verdicts, and it is limited to a Tap-kind tool in a Z drill cycle. My probes found one case where the re-read now passes a real collision, though: the shank. That is the one blocker.

### What looks good
- One derivation. `tap_core::core_tool` calls `tool_law::cutting_radius`, the same function the program sim (#713) sweeps. There is no second formula.
- The scope is narrow. Only `ToolKind::Tap` is re-read, only in `OpParams::Drill` with no cross holes, and only `Warning::Gouge`. Rapids (`RapidInStock`), `ShankHit` and `HolderHit` from the full-size run are kept. The Thread op (and open #1099) is untouched, so no excuse stacks there.
- Bad pitch is handled cleanly. If `cutting_radius` has no core, or the core is not finite, not positive, or not under the full diameter, `core_tool` returns `None` and the full verdict stands. AddTool already refuses a negative or NaN pitch. No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in non-test code.
- The provenance line on `tap_core.rs` names ISO 724. There is a decision record, a `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #266`. No goldens, snapshots, CHANGELOG or process files changed.
- Interplay with #1220's `wall_excuse` (`crates/sim/src/verify/hole_wall.rs:55`): it runs inside the core judge as well. It is capped at the facet sagitta (`WALL_SAG` = 0.05 mm) of a declared round hole, so the most it adds on top of the core reading is the tessellation chord, not a second radius.

### Local results (trial merge with main `0757563d`: already up to date, no conflicts)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` | 146 passed |
| `tap_sim` | 7 passed |
| `drill_reach` 6, `drill_reach_fit` 3, `drill_prior` 12, `drill_prior_kinds` 4, `drilling_axial` 7, `tapping_mode` 4 | all passed |
| `solid_law` 4, `solid_law_goldens` 5, `hole_wall_flats` 4, `coarse_contain` 1, `blind_floor` 7, `face_holes` 3 | all passed |
| `stock_sim_document` 9, `tool_law` 4, `tool_body_drill_probe` 5, `posting` 17 | all passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| Pinning test on main's `generate.rs` | `a_tap_in_a_tap_drill_hole_carries_no_blocking_warning` fails (Gouge at 1, 2), as the body says |

Probe readings: local throwaway tests, not pushed. The M6x1 catalog tap, a block with a 12 mm blind square hole, and the op's cached warnings after the PR.

| Case | Warnings | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Ø5 hole (tap drill) | none | correct |
| Ø4.88 hole (under D1 4.917) | Gouge 1, 2 | convicted |
| Ø4.6 hole | Gouge 1, 2 | convicted |
| Tapped 0.2 mm / 3 mm past the hole floor | Gouge 1, 2 | convicted |
| Off centre 0.6 mm (more than the 0.54 thread depth) / 0.1 mm / in solid metal | Gouge 1, 2 | convicted |
| Pitch 7 (no core) | Gouge 1, 2 | full verdict stands |
| Ø8 shank, 4 mm flute, hole record Ø8 | ShankHit 1 | convicted |
| **Ø6 shank, 4 mm flute, hole record Ø6 (model Ø5), 12 mm deep** | **none** (program sim 0 cells) | **passes; main blocks it with Gouge 1, 2** |

### Requested before merge
1. **A shank collision on an acquitted move is lost** (`crates/app/src/operation/tap_core.rs:45`). The solid law reports a move once: `Gouge` when the fluted edge hits, else `ShankHit` (`crates/sim/src/verify/solid.rs:145-152`). The band-reach law (c) only flags a shank wider than the cutter it judges. So in the full-diameter run, a Ø6 shank on a Ø6 tap never gets its own `ShankHit`: the `Gouge` on that move hides it. The core run does see it (Ø6 shank against a Ø4.917 cutter in a Ø5 hole). But `acquit` keeps only the core run's `Gouge`s, so its `ShankHit` is thrown away.
   Result: a tap whose shank is as wide as its major diameter, with a 4 mm thread length (DIN 371 style), fed 12 mm into a Ø5 hole, posts with no warning. The shank rubs 8 mm of the hole's thread crests. `drill_reach::shank_fits` does not catch it when the hole record states the thread's nominal Ø6 (a natural way to list an M6 hole), because it judges the record, not the model. On main the same case is blocked.
   Fix: for each move whose `Gouge` is dropped, carry the core run's body verdicts on that move (`ShankHit`, `HolderHit`, and `SweepHit`/`FixtureHit` if raised) into `warns`, deduplicated. Pin it with a test: catalog tap with `flute_len: 4.0, shank_d: 6.0`, hole record `radius: 3.0`, model half-width 2.5 → a blocking `ShankHit` (or `Gouge`).

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- `core_tool` does not check the cycle. A Tap-kind tool in an explicit `CycleChoice::Drill`/`Peck` op is re-read at its core as well. Today that case still blocks through `RapidInStock { at: 2 }`, so nothing passes, but `matches!(cycle, Tap | FloatingTap | Auto)` would match the intent ("a tap rides a tap-drill hole").
- `a_tap_deeper_than_its_hole_is_still_convicted` and `a_tap_with_no_hole_under_it_is_still_convicted` assert `!warns.is_empty()`. Asserting a `Gouge` (as the under-D1 test does) would stop an unrelated warning from keeping them green.
- At Ø4.88 the program sim finds 0 gouge cells while verify convicts. That is a sim resolution limit from #713, not this PR, and verify holds the post.
- `generate.rs` grows 3284 → 3291 lines (already far over ~400). The `};` closing `ctx` at line 2841 is indented one level off.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
